title.narrative: Increasing LGBTI people's opportunities for economic and social inclusion in Honduras

description.narrative: Website Marginalized low-income groups in Tegucigalpa and Comayagela face many obstacles to improving their quality of life. Centro para el Desarrollo y la Cooperacin (SOMOS CDC) provides vocational and microenterprise training for at-risk youth from Tegucigalpa and Comayagela, and works to advance the basic rights of marginalized groups in Honduras. At the IAF, we support community-led solutions to strengthen economic opportunity and social inclusion in Honduras. SOMOS CDC?s activities encourage participants to develop small businesses and increase their access to employment to ensure meaningful opportunities for communities to thrive. This grant is part of the IAF?s efforts to address the root causes of irregular migration in Central America. Amendment FY20 This amendment provides SOMOS CDC with an additional two years and $160,100 to provide youth entrepreneurs with technical assistance and access to a revolving loan fund. As part of the amendment, SOMOS CDC is mobilizing an additional $235,600 in counterpart funding to the grant agreement. Amendment FY24 This amendment provides SOMOS CDC with an additional 24 months and $181,485 to provide technical support to small businesses recuperating from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, address long-term barriers to employment for vulnerable groups, and strengthen local efforts to address violence and discrimination. As part of the amendment, SOMOS CDC is mobilizing an additional $206,835 in counterpart resources to the grant agreement.
